why: Revenue growth of 4.7% -> 12.7% -> 13.5% is the NZAS/Tiwai smelter's third potline coming back on line after the Feb-2025 Meridian demand-response curtailment, plus a one-off ~16,000-tonne wind-farm turbine cargo boost and a log-export surge from a wind-throw weather event in FY26 -- not a durable step-change in the underlying ~3% volume-CAGR port business. Management itself guides FY2027 volumes 'broadly in line with FY26' (i.e. flat) and explicitly flags the loss of the one-off project cargo, declining to give firm FY27 financial guidance.
watch: FY2027 trade volumes: flat guide is the company's own bar - any miss confirms the FY26 pop was one-off, not an acceleration
Tiwai/NZAS wharf volumes (24% of FY26 tonnage): a repeat Meridian demand-response curtailment in a dry hydro year would cut this again, as it did in FY25
Price NZ$8.77 vs IV NZ$6.32 (-27.9%, 'expensive' tier) and vs base-case entry price NZ$3.51 (15% hurdle) - the stock is priced well above even the bull-case DCF output
Port Planning Exercise Stage 1/2 results (due late Sept 2026) and any Stage 3 'transformation' capex program that could relever the currently low (0.6x EBITDA) balance sheet
